ambiguities.description: The chunk directs inquiries to a contact but the contact's name, email and phone are cut off, so bidders cannot tell to whom and by what channel questions must be sent.

The module list is presented as the City's current Tyler Technologies configuration, not explicitly as required functionality of the new system; a bidder would ask whether all listed modules (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and approvals) must be replaced one-for-one.

The text states the City currently has five users but does not say whether five is the licensed user count required in the new system or whether growth must be accommodated; a bidder would ask for the required user licensing quantity.

The schedule says the City will make every effort to adhere to it, so it is unclear whether the proposal submission deadline of August 28, 2025 and the interview date are firm or may shift; a bidder would ask whether dates are binding and how changes will be communicated.

The RFP does not define what counts as a trade secret or how the City will treat marked information, so a bidder cannot tell which technical or pricing-adjacent content is safe to mark; the bidder would ask what criteria the City applies and whether marking affects evaluation.

The City's standard contract with terms and conditions is only 'available upon request', so bidders cannot see the terms they must accept before submitting; the bidder would ask for a copy of the standard contract and whether it will be attached as an exhibit.

The text says the City may leave open later negotiation and amendment of specific contract provisions, yet also states that any modified terms submitted with a proposal will be disregarded and can render the proposal nonresponsive; the bidder would ask how exceptions can be raised without risking rejection.

The text requires modification requests to be raised "during the question period" per Section 2.3, but the dates and procedure of that question period are not given here; a bidder would ask for the question-period deadline and the required format for submitting a proposed modification.

The City states it may exercise discretion not to consider any proposed modifications, without saying whether or how a Respondent is notified of the outcome before the proposal deadline; a bidder would ask whether acceptance of a requested modification will be confirmed before proposals are due.

The text allows exceptions for "general inquiries before submission and after status updates" but does not define who may be contacted, through what channel, or what counts as a general inquiry versus a prohibited communication; a bidder would ask which contact point and topics are permitted during the evaluation period.

The disqualification exception turns on the City's subjective judgment that a communication is "harmless and unintentional" and in the City's best interest, with no process for the respondent to explain or cure a communication; a bidder would ask whether there is a notice-and-cure procedure.

The City may reject any proposal on the basis of "fit, form, and function" without defining those terms, so bidders cannot tell what would disqualify a proposal beyond cost and stated specifications; the bidder would ask what criteria define fit, form and function.

The criterion "Technical support during software implementation and ongoing" is truncated and does not say what is evaluated (response times, support hours, staffing, cost) or what period "ongoing" covers; a bidder would ask what content and service levels must be described under this 25% criterion.

The text says submissions deemed noncompliant or technically unqualified will not be considered but does not define the compliance or qualification threshold; a bidder would ask what minimum qualifications or compliance checklist determines disqualification.

The text says no single requirement automatically disqualifies a respondent, yet non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to reject a proposal entirely; a bidder would ask which requirements are pass/fail and how partial compliance is scored.

The page limit is stated as "should not exceed 20 pages" (desired) while the surrounding text says respondents are "required to adhere" to the guidelines; it is unclear whether exceeding 20 pages (plus allowances) makes a proposal non-compliant. The bidder would ask whether the 20-page limit is a pass/fail requirement.

The hard copy must be "received" at the address by the deadline, but the text does not say whether the mailed PO Box copy and the street-address copy are alternatives or whether both must be sent; it also does not state whether the hard copy may arrive after the email timestamp. The bidder would ask which address to use and whether the hard copy must physically arrive by 4:00 PM PST on August 28, 2025.

The text allows post-opening withdrawal only for "good cause" without defining what qualifies, so a bidder cannot tell whether a mistake or changed circumstances would be accepted; the bidder would ask what criteria the City applies to "good cause".

The text refers to "the required elements outlined below" and "additional details required for each proposal section" that are not contained in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell from this text what the full set of required proposal elements is; the bidder would ask for the complete list of required proposal sections and their contents.

It is unclear who qualifies as an "authorized signature" (e.g., an officer of the firm, a specific title, or a notarized signatory) and which attachments require one; the bidder would ask what signatory authority and form of signature are acceptable.

The text does not say whether the listed response elements are mandatory or merely suggested, since the lead-in only says respondents "should" address the goals; a bidder would ask whether omitting any element (e.g., virtual demos) makes the proposal non-responsive.

It is unclear what "account number customization abilities" covers (customer-defined account numbering scheme, format, length, or numbering of the vendor's own accounts), which affects how the design and demo are presented.

The July 1, 2026 go-live is stated as the City's goal, not a contractual deadline, and no implementation start date or contract award date is given, so the bidder cannot size the implementation schedule; the bidder would ask whether July 1, 2026 is a firm requirement and when implementation is expected to begin.

The text does not say whether the account manager is required or merely an option, nor whether that role must be dedicated or on-site; the bidder would ask what level of account management commitment is expected.

The chunk refers to "this information" without defining what firm information and qualifications must be provided for each company; the bidder would ask what specific items (licenses, references, financials, resumes) are required per firm.

The City expresses a "desire" for participation by minority-, women-, disabled- and small-business enterprises but sets no goal, percentage, or required form of evidence, so a bidder cannot tell whether a specific subcontracting commitment or documentation is expected.

The text does not define what counts as "recent" experience (e.g., within the last three or five years), which affects which references and projects the bidder can cite; the bidder would ask for the cutoff period.

It is unclear what qualifies as a "local referral" (within the City of Colfax area, the county, or the region) and whether the in-person demonstration is a scored expectation; the bidder would ask for the geographic definition and whether the demonstration is required at bid time or later.

The text requires reimbursable expenses to be capped but does not state a cap amount or whether the City sets a maximum; a bidder would ask what cap level is acceptable or whether the cap is at the Respondent's discretion.

The text requires an estimate of costs/fees for "additional applications and/or vendors" without defining which applications or vendors are contemplated; a bidder would ask what additional applications/vendors must be priced.

The required insurance types are open-ended ("including, but not limited to") and no minimum coverage limits or additional-insured requirements are stated here, so the bidder cannot price the coverage; the bidder would ask which coverages and limits are required.

Attachment G asks for documentation of financial-data protection and secure access controls without naming a standard, framework or format, so the bidder cannot tell what evidence will be accepted; the bidder would ask which standard or format the documentation must follow.

The chunk refers to "required items" and "optional items" in the scope of work without identifying them here; a bidder would ask which deliverables are mandatory versus optional, since that determines the proposal content and price.

The scope does not say whether the 12 months of post-implementation support is included in the base price or is a separately priced option, nor when that period starts (go-live vs. contract signature). The bidder would ask how to price and schedule it.

The text does not define the volume or format of the prior 5 years of data to be imported, nor who supplies and cleans it. The bidder would ask for data volumes, source systems and file formats to size the migration effort.

The July 1, 2026 completion date is stated as a "goal" rather than a firm deadline, so it is unclear whether it is a binding milestone subject to penalties or an aspirational target; the bidder would ask whether the date is mandatory.

The project start is described only as "soon after awarding the contract and finalizing negotiations," leaving the start date and any notice-to-proceed period undefined; the bidder would ask for the expected award date and contract start date to build the schedule.

The text requires a capped reimbursable expense amount but gives no ceiling or basis for the cap, so bidders cannot tell whether the City expects a specific maximum or a respondent-proposed figure; the bidder would ask whether a maximum cap value or methodology is prescribed.

It is unclear how the 'Total price proposal' differs from the 'Total price for all services and deliverables' plus the reimbursable cap, i.e. whether the total price proposal is their sum or a separate figure; the bidder would ask how the three amounts relate.

The references must be for "similar services ... as outlined herein", but this chunk does not define what counts as similar; the bidder would ask what scope or service categories qualify as similar references.

The form requires written notice of relocation outside the United States but sets no timeframe or recipient, so a bidder cannot tell whether notice must precede the move and to whom it must be addressed.

The certification lists the same audit-opinion statement twice, so it is unclear whether both boxes must be checked or whether one is a drafting duplicate; the bidder would ask which representation is required.

The certification does not define what counts as a "material change" triggering the 15-day notice, nor whether the notice obligation continues after contract award; the bidder would ask for the standard to apply.

The required coverage limits, additional-insured status and certificate form for the workers compensation and commercial general liability policies are not stated, so the bidder cannot price the insurance or know whether its current coverage qualifies; the bidder would ask what limits and endorsements are required.

The text does not specify what form or level of detail the documentation of financial-data protection and access controls must take (e.g., policies, certifications, diagrams), nor which financial data or systems are in scope, so a bidder cannot judge what evidence will be accepted.

Conflicting requirements R099 and R139: One requires notice to the City within 30 days of material changes to the financial certification, while the other requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days.
